transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood CCS), Tom Alvarez (NorthBridge CISO), Sara Kim (Head of IT), Rachel Nguyen (Compliance), Ethan Park (DevOps), Olivia Morse (Legal)

Summary: quick SOC2/ISO posture review + next steps to share artifacts and schedule tech deep dive

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan with Redwood, and with me are Priya our solution engineer and Marcus from customer compliance support. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Tom: Good thanks, Tom here. We wanted to run through your SOC 2 and ISO posture, see what artifacts you can provide and how Redwood maps to our control set.
[00:15] Jordan: Absolutely. High level we'll cover what reports we can share, trust center access, controls mapping, SSO/RBAC options, audit logs, data residency, and encryption KMS options. Priya will jump in on technical pieces.
[00:25] Priya: Hi all. Quick note — transcription might miss a few product names, so apologies if something shows up weird.
[00:30] Sara: No worries. One ask up front: we need both SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO27001 summary. Is that available?
[00:36] Jordan: Yes, we can share SOC 2 Type II and our ISO 27001 cert summary through the Redwood Trust Center. We'll send a link and an NDA/protected access if needed.
[00:45] Rachel: Great. Also we'd like a controls mapping — your controls to our policy identifiers — for the audit team.
[00:49] Jordan: Understood. Priya, Marcus, we can produce a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to typical frameworks, and we can do a custom mapping to NorthBridge's control IDs.
[00:58] Marcus: Yep, we've done that for several customers. We usually provide an initial mapping and then iterate based on the customer's baseline.
[01:05] Tom: For SSO, we use Okta with SAML 2.0, and we also want SCIM for user provisioning eventually. What does Redwood support?
[01:13] Priya: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning; OIDC can be supported for some flows. RBAC is role-based and integrated with SSO; we expose roles and can also support just-in-time provisioning. There are some fine-grained permissions for project vs org-level access.
[01:26] Ethan: On the infra side, we need audit logs streamed to our SIEM (Splunk) and retention for 7 years for certain events. Can you ship logs or provide streaming?
[01:35] Marcus: We provide audit logs via the Trust Center and can stream structured logs via secure ingestion endpoints or S3 export. Default retention in hosted is 90 days, longer retention is available as an add-on or via Dedicated/Private deployments.
[01:46] Sara: So for hosted, retention is 90 days — but we could do dedicated for extended retention?
[01:50] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated or Private deployments allow configurable retention and retention policies per-customer; we can also arrange long-term log export to your S3 for archival and compliance.
[01:58] Olivia: From a legal perspective, we also need encryption at rest and key management details. Do you bring your own keys (BYOK) or customer-managed keys?
[02:07] Priya: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we provide managed encryption but can integrate with dedicated KMS for enterprise customers via a customer KMS tie-in. We'll send details on supported KMS providers and the key rotation procedures.
[02:20] Tom: Data residency is another big one — some PHI must stay in specific regions. What options do you have for region isolation?
[02:27] Jordan: We have region selection in Hosted where requests are routed to a region; for strict isolation we recommend Dedicated pools in a specific region or Private VPC where you control networking and residency. We'll need to map exactly which data types and endpoints are in scope.
[02:39] Rachel: On the controls mapping, do you map to ISO 27001 Annex A directly? We want to see how your policies map to our internal controls and Annex A clauses.
[02:47] Marcus: Yes, our standard mapping includes SOC 2 criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A, and common regs like HIPAA-related controls. We'll provide the mapping as a spreadsheet with reference links to policies and evidence artifacts.
[02:58] Ethan: For network architecture, can you provide a sample diagram for Dedicated and Private? We need to validate firewall rules and peering.
[03:05] Priya: Absolutely — we'll share network diagrams and the recommended IP ranges, NAT behavior, and peering docs. For Private deployments we support customer-managed subnets and VPC peering; for Dedicated we provide isolated tenant pools with peering options.
[03:18] Tom: How about auditability of model changes and model provenance? We need to show controls that models used for inference are from approved versions.
[03:26] Jordan: We have model versioning and release notes in the console; for Dedicated/Private you can pin model versions and we'll retain model artifacts and provenance logs. For Hosted we keep version history and can export model change logs to your SIEM.
[03:38] Rachel: Are penetration test reports available?
[03:41] Marcus: We can share redacted pentest summaries and remediation timelines. Full reports may be under NDA.
[03:47] Olivia: About encryption transit — TLS 1.2/1.3, mutual TLS for backend ingestion?
[03:52] Priya: We support TLS 1.2/1.3; mutual TLS is available for privileged backend ingestion endpoints and for the S3 export path. We can also set up IP allowlists.
[04:02] Tom: Any gaps you typically see when customers ask for 7+ years of logs?
[04:07] Marcus: Hosted customers typically rely on exports to S3 for long-term retention; gaps are usually in log normalization and indexing costs. We'll propose an archival pattern: export to your S3 and run lifecycle policies.
[04:18] Ethan: For SCIM provisioning, do you support groups and custom attributes?
[04:22] Priya: Yes, groups and custom attributes are supported; we'll show the attribute mapping in the SCIM doc.
[04:28] Sara: From compliance, we need to know your incident response SLA and notification cadence if a security event affects our data.
[04:35] Jordan: Our incident response includes 24/7 detection and notification within agreed SLA tiers; for enterprise customers we provide a primary incident contact and post-incident reports. We'll include the IR playbook excerpt in the trust center.
[04:46] Tom: For your trust center access — is that self-serve or controlled?
[04:50] Marcus: It's controlled. We'll provision read-only access to the trust center for your compliance team and can gate certain artifacts behind an NDA.
[04:58] Rachel: We will want the SOC 2 bridge letters and any compensating controls docs for the last 12 months.
[05:04] Jordan: We'll provide the bridge letters where applicable and list compensating controls in the mapping spreadsheet.
[05:10] Olivia: Are you certifying for ISO 27701 or anything around privacy?
[05:14] Marcus: Right now we have ISO 27001; ISO 27701 is on our roadmap but not yet certified. We'll note that in the artifacts.
[05:21] Tom: Competitors question — how do you compare on audit artifacts to providers like OpenAI or Anthropic?
[05:28] Jordan: We try to provide enterprise-ready artifacts — more similar to a cloud vendor approach with a Trust Center and dedicated account support. We emphasize Dedicated and Private deployment options that give stronger isolation and control compared to generic hosted endpoints.
[05:40] Sara: For the controls mapping, our auditors also want evidence URLs or timestamps for when remediation happened. Can you include evidence pointers?
[05:47] Marcus: Yes, each mapping row will include evidence reference (doc link or timestamp) where feasible. Some live systems data will be redacted; we'll provide sanitized logs or screenshots under NDA.
[05:59] Ethan: If we go Dedicated, what's the onboarding timeline for SOC/ISO compliance review?
[06:04] Jordan: Typically Dedicated onboarding is 4-8 weeks depending on network setup and IP allowlist approvals; Private can take longer. We can provide a project plan after the technical deep dive.
[06:14] Tom: Ok let's talk about KMS specifics — which providers and key wrap methods are supported?
[06:19] Priya: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for BYOK integrations. For Private we also support hardware security modules via partner HSMs. Key wrap uses AES-GCM for envelope encryption; we can share crypto details in the KMS integration doc.
[06:33] Rachel: Retention and deletion policies — if we request deletion for a dataset, how is that handled?
[06:38] Marcus: We have a deletion workflow. For Hosted, deletion requests are processed and we purge training/derivative stores as per policy; for Dedicated/Private you can configure stricter deletion and retention behaviors and we provide a deletion certificate. We'll include the process and SLAs in the docs.
[06:51] Olivia: Anything about third-party subprocessors and their certs?
[06:54] Jordan: Yes, subprocessors and their security posture are listed in the trust center; we include SOC 2/ISO status where applicable.
[07:01] Tom: Sounds good. Rachel, any other compliance asks?
[07:04] Rachel: We want to review sample audit logs and a sample controls mapping before we sign off. Also the legal team wants the BAAs/PHI handling notes.
[07:12] Olivia: We'll need a draft BAA.
[07:14] Jordan: We can provide a BAA template; Marcus and legal will follow up.
[07:18] Priya: Next technical step — should we schedule a deep-dive focused on network/infra and log export with Ethan and your infra team?
[07:24] Ethan: Yes, prefer next Tue or Wed.
[07:27] Jordan: We'll propose Tuesday. Priya will send a calendar invite.
[07:31] Tom: One small item — does Redwood keep an immutable audit trail for admin actions? Our auditors like immutability.
[07:38] Marcus: We keep append-only audit logs for admin actions; for Dedicated/Private these can be exported to your S3 and we can support object immutability via bucket settings.
[07:48] Jordan: Ok let's recap: Jordan will share SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary via trust center link; Priya will send controls mapping and KMS/encryption notes; Marcus will include pentest summaries and evidence pointers; schedule tech deep-dive for next Tue with Ethan; customer to provide data residency targets and network diagram.
[08:05] Rachel: That works. Thanks everyone.
[08:08] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts and invite.
[47:50] [call ends]

Notes: transcript has crosstalk and some minor transcription errors typical of Fireflies exports (product names may be slightly off).
